title: Graceful degradation, prefetch shim, and model fallback protocol for memory pressure
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Under bursty traffic and long-context requests, the serving runtime can exceed GPU memory headroom during continuous batching + KV prefetching. Existing hard eviction strategies reduce throughput and increase latency spikes. We need a coordinated, low-latency recovery strategy that avoids full task failure or costly restarts while preserving as much utility as possible for end-users.

Goal: Implement a graded fallback protocol that combines a lightweight prefetch shim, memory headroom estimator, adaptive batch thinning, and deterministic model fallback paths to keep requests returning useful output rather than failing. The protocol should be compatible with streaming responses and preserve ordering and consistency guarantees for multi-request sessions.

Key ideas: 1) Prefetch shim: a runtime layer that caps/grades KV prefetch size per request using request importance score and current memory headroom. It can request "minimal" prefixes first and issue background prefetches if headroom improves. 2) Headroom estimator: continuous metric (mem.headroom_ratio) combining reserved buffer, fragmentation estimate, and pending allocation forecast. 3) Batch thinning: when headroom falls under threshold, shrink in-flight batch size gracefully by deferring lower-priority requests and issuing partial outputs for affected requests (e.g., truncated continuation or condensed summary). 4) Graded model fallback: deterministic map from model variant -> smaller/quantized variant -> condensed-output generator model. Fallback selection considers latency SLO, cost tier, and user-specified degradation tolerance. 5) Retry protocol: soft-retry with jitter and backoff for requests that were deferred; for streaming requests, send a partial token marker and schedule resume attempt to continue generation when capacity returns. 6) Observability & safety: surface events in Console (per-request memory events, fallback reasons, and user-visible degradation messages). Add rollback/canary config flags for deployment experiments.

Non-goals: Replacing global eviction policies entirely or compromising KV correctness. This ticket should integrate with existing eviction mechanisms and not remove current safeguards.
updates: 2026-03-09: Spike completed — implemented a memory headroom estimator prototype in staging using a combination of CUDA memoryUsed, allocator fragmentation tags, and recent allocation deltas. Headroom estimate correlated with OOM incidents with 0.86 AUC in the test trace set.

2026-03-10: Prefetch shim design reviewed with PM and infra. Decided on 3 prefetch levels: minimal (prompt-only), eager (prompt + first N tokens), full (prompt + full window). Default mapping: minimal under 0.25 headroom, eager 0.25-0.5, full above 0.5. Added canary flag pref:runtime.prefetch_shim to gate rollout.

2026-03-11: Implemented batch-thinning hook in the scheduler that can drop low-priority requests from a batch and mark them as deferred. Integration test with continuous-batching harness shows throughput drop of 8% but reduces peak memory from 28GB to 23GB in heavy long-context scenario.

2026-03-11: Prototype graded fallback chain: rdx-13b.fp16 -> rdx-13b.8bit -> rdx-7b.8bit-condensed. Fallback selection code added to routing layer; fallback triggered only when headroom < 0.12 and immediate recovery is required to avoid an unrecoverable allocation failure.

2026-03-12: Added streaming-compatible partial-output protocol: on fallback, send a "partial_continuation" marker and metadata explaining degradation (variant used, truncated tokens). UX/PM reviewed messaging for user-facing clients.

2026-03-12: Opened PR #5482 with runtime changes and feature flag. Load tests in staging (replicated customer corpus) show 98% reduction in hard task failures and median latency increase of +45ms for degraded requests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5482

2026-03-12: Next steps: expand test coverage for session resume flow, add metrics to Console (mem.headroom_ratio, fallback.rate, deferred.request.count), and schedule canary rollout to 5% of traffic for Dedicated tier next week.
acceptance_criteria: Headroom estimator available as a runtime metric (mem.headroom_ratio) and shown in staging dashboards
Prefetch shim implemented and gated behind pref:runtime.prefetch_shim, with three prefetch levels behaving as specified
Batch-thinning and deferred request flow implemented, with session resume tested for streaming requests
Graded model fallback chain configurable per model with deterministic selection rules
Runbook updated with steps to diagnose and revert degraded fallback behavior
Canary rollout executed to 5% traffic in Dedicated and no increase in customer-visible error rate observed
